processing_notes: Source states: 'Le cholera. Apres les epidemies de cholera observees en 1998, 1999 et 2001 a Brazzaville et a Pointe-Noire, aucun cas n'a ete notifie sur l'ensemble du territoire de 2001 a 2005. -- PRESENCE SUSPECTED, NOT ESTABLISHED (confidence 0.4). The only source naming 2001 as an epidemic year is this WHO CCS sentence, which in the same breath says no case was notified nationwide from 2001 to 2005. Against presence: Congo is absent from every cholera notification table in all 51 WER 2001 issues and all 51 WER 2002 issues, absent from the WER 'Cholera, 2001' annual table, and has no 2001 value in WHO GHO; the CCS list also skips 2000 (9 cases / 2 deaths in WHO data), so '2001' may be a typo for 2000. Weakly for: Pointe-Noire stayed on the WHO IHR infected-areas list throughout 2001 (WER 2001 No 9, 19, 27, 36), but under the list criteria (WER 2001 No 13 p.100) areas stay listed until freedom is notified, so this is carry-over from 1997-99. Recorded so that 2001 is not written as a zero without new evidence; not a data row.' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.

source: UNICEF helps respond to cholera outbreak in Pointe Noire 3 February 1998 (UNICEF press release via ReliefWeb)
processing_notes: Source states: 'Cases of severe diarrhea were first reported in the area of Mvouti, 150 km northeast of Pointe Noire, as early as June 1997 ... The outbreak moved to Madingo-Kayes and then further south, with the first case of severe diarrhea reported in Pointe Noire on 7 November 1997. A total of 1,019 cases and 36 deaths were reported from the earlier outbreaks in Mvouti and Madingo-Kayes. -- COUNT KNOWN BUT NOT COMMITTED AS A DATA ROW: 1,019 severe-diarrhoea cases / 36 deaths in Mvouti and Madingo-Kayes districts (Kouilou), June-early November 1997, i.e. the start of the 1997-98 coastal cholera epidemic before it reached Pointe-Noire (cholera later laboratory-confirmed by WHO in 'the area'). Held back because (1) >1000 cases requires a second independent source and none was found (OCHA Jan-Feb 1998 sitrep, WHO DONs 3/10 Feb 1998, WFP and IRIN 1998 reports and a targeted web search give no Mvouti/Madingo-Kayes figure; DON 10 Feb 1998 says 'Complete figures are not available'), (2) it is a syndromic 'severe diarrhea' count reported before laboratory confirmation, and (3) it is almost four times WHO's national 1997 total (275 cases / 60 deaths). Window end 1997-11-06 = day before Pointe-Noire's first case (the source's 'earlier outbreaks'); the figure's own as-of date is not given (release 3 Feb 1998). Lead for Agent 5: seek corroboration in MoH/WHO-AFRO 1997-98 reports.' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.
